notes.note: The clerk speaks to two travellers (تُسَافِرَانِ، مِنْ فَضْلِكُمَا) but asks for جَوَازَ السَّفَر in the singular; correct as a generic 'the passport', but جَوَازَيِ السَّفَر / جَوَازَاتِ السَّفَر would match the two people better (Daniel then hands over two).

With the compound subject 'Daniel and Layla' these verbs are glossed '(he) went' / '(he) arrived', while days 51, 53, 55, 56 gloss the same pattern '(they) will … (verb first: singular)'. Not wrong (literal 3ms), but the explanatory gloss would help the learner and keep the course consistent.

Counted nouns after 3–10 are left in pause form (خَمْسَ دَرَجَات، خَمْسَ جُمَل، ثَلَاث سَاعَات، ثَلَاثَةُ أَشْخَاص) while counted nouns after 11–99 show -an (ضَيْفًا، دِينَارًا، دَرَجَةً). Acceptable as pause style, but if the house rule 'endings on counted nouns' is meant to cover 3–10 too, the genitive -in (دَرَجَاتٍ، جُمَلٍ، سَاعَاتٍ، أَشْخَاصٍ) would be the consistent form.

'In standard Arabic the day is an ordinal followed by min' is a little absolute: cardinal dates (الْخَامِس / خَمْسَة نُوفَمْبِر read as numbers) are also heard in MSA media. The wrong form here is fine as colloquial; softening to 'usually' would match the course's other notes.
هٰذَا الْهَرَم كَبِير وَقَدِيم جِدًّا: جِدًّا strictly follows قَدِيم; 'very big and very old' is a free reading. 'This pyramid is big and very old' is closer, or move جِدًّا to keep the English.
Culture fact: May in Cairo is already hot (often 33°C+, khamasin season), so 'the weather is pleasant in October and May' is generous; March/April or November would be safer.

summary: Read the whole export for days 51–60 (weekend plans with lan, invitations and li- of purpose, weather, seasons with yakūnu, months, dates with ordinals, airport, hotel, booking with hollow verbs, asking for help with object suffixes), checking every Arabic string against its syntax (lan/an/lam moods, kāna/yakūnu/laysa predicates, number–noun agreement and tamyīz, iḍāfa definiteness, dual forms after prepositions, verb–subject agreement in verb-first sentences, imperatives to one/two/several people), every literal and English translation, every quiz answer key and mistakes pair, the grammar notes and pronunciation questions, and the seg/tap glosses. About 330 Arabic strings (sentences, mistakes pairs, 150 dialogue lines, 10 readings, quiz options) and about 2,600 seg/tap glosses checked: 0 errors found. The story timeline is also consistent (party Friday 7 Nov, week test Sunday 9 Nov, Wednesday 10 Dec, flight Thursday after 1 Dec, Petra Saturday). Six notes for the owner: a singular passport asked of two people, '(he) went/arrived' glosses on compound subjects, pause form on counted nouns after 3–10, one slightly absolute date note, the scope of جِدًّا in d51s5, and May described as pleasant in Cairo.
